bugs.description: Footnote 20 verisimilitude probit models (mod_UK line 197-199, mod_US line 201-203) pass weights as `...$w1`, but the prepared data has no column w1 (01_Prepare data.R creates only `w`). `$w1` returns NULL, so these two bayesglm models run unweighted, unlike every other model in the deposit. Not a target.

bugs.description: Inside the country loop (i = 1 US, i = 2 UK) the counterfactual data for the change-in-probability simulations is `tmp_0 <- tmp_1 <- data`, the combined UK+US data, instead of the country subset `tmp` used to fit the model. Each country's effects in Figure A4 (Open_explore.pdf) are averaged over both samples' covariates. Numerically small. Not a target.

class_reason: All six targets match the printed values to rounding (T1-T4 to 2 decimals as the pre-registered draw Mean, T5/T6 exactly), with negative WHO coefficients and code p < .01. Targets came from the PREREG labelled fallback for 03 because the full 03 exceeded available memory; 01 ran unchanged.
confidence_reason: Script-matched to rounding with the authors' pinned ebal and logr; the only deviation is the pre-registered fallback, which by construction uses the same random draws as the full 03 (refit in robustness.R gives identical Mean).
uncertainties: The full 03_Estimate main models.R did not complete here (OOM at 3.3 GB RSS with about 3.1 GB available on the shared machine); targets come from the PREREG fallback. Outputs of 03's simulations, 04, 06, 07, 08 (Figures 3-6, A2-A4, Table A9, Estimates_numbers.csv) were not produced, so figure-based claims (e.g. WHO change in probability 0.13 UK, 0.11 US) were not checked.

Memory gate: the brief says wait if free memory < 3 GB; the 'free' column stayed below 3 GB because about 3.9 GB was shared/tmpfs plus page cache from other processes, so MemAvailable >= 3 GB was used as the gate.
Secondary (not targets): 20 of 20 WHO cells in Tables 2-3 match the paper; 'leave open' proportions match: True (outputs/secondary_check.json, Choices_prop from the unchanged 02 run).

Our regenerated Table 2 prints stars on UK All-neighbors Gender (-0.47$^{*}$) and Ideology (1.76$^{**}$), which the published table shows without stars (PREREG inconsistency 6). Values match; only the stars differ, which suggests a typesetting difference in the published table. Not a target. US Ideology (do not know), Threatened neighbors also gives -7.81$^{**}$ as printed (SD prints as 0.00).

Unverified observation, 01_Prepare data.R lines 138-142: BES LR stays a factor after mapvalues and becomes character when rbind-ed with the numeric CCES LR, so the ebalance formula's LR >= 0.0 & LR <= 0.3 and LR >= 0.7 are string comparisons for UK target rows. In this C.UTF-8 locale they agree with the numeric comparison on all 2139 BES rows (outputs/code_checks.txt Check 1); under a locale whose collation ignores the minus sign (for example en_US) '-99' could sort above '0.7'. Not testable here (only C/POSIX locales installed). Weights here reproduce the targets exactly, so no effect on this run.

Unverified observation, 01_Prepare data.R line 162: the 10,000 target-population rows are drawn with sample() without the CCES/BES survey weights, so the population weights carried in t_data$w are not used in entropy balancing (they are used only in 02's population descriptives). Could be intended; not a confirmed bug.
pvalue in 03 uses df = nrow(data) of the combined UK+US data rather than the country N; with N about 1600 this has no practical effect on stars.

The tool issued the first fallback launch twice; the duplicate failed immediately on a transient missing plyr. All reported numbers come from the single successful fallback run and the sequential robustness runs.
